metadata.Initiative / Programme: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689), incl. Art. 4 AI literacy
metadata.Description: Horizontal EU regulation on AI; Art. 4 requires providers and deployers to take measures to ensure/support AI literacy of staff; certain education uses are classified high-risk (Annex III).

summary: The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is a horizontal regulation establishing a legal framework for artificial intelligence systems in the European Union. Article 4 specifically requires providers and deployers of AI systems to take appropriate measures to ensure and support AI literacy, including training staff and developing specific curricula where appropriate.

inclusion.reason: This initiative qualifies for inclusion under the 'Issued by a national or sub-national government' route (specifically, a supranational intergovernmental body - the EU). The regulation is directly applicable law issued by the European Union institutions. It includes explicit AI literacy requirements in Article 4, mandating that providers and deployers implement measures to ensure/support AI literacy of staff, which satisfies the mandatory AI-literacy requirement.

metadata.Initiative / Programme: EC–OECD AI Literacy Framework (AILit) "Empowering Learners for the Age of AI"
metadata.Description: Joint European Commission–OECD framework defining AI literacy competences across four domains (Engage with, Create with, Manage and Design/Shape AI), with learning scenarios; basis for PISA 2029 MAIL.

summary: The EC–OECD AI Literacy Framework (AILit) is a joint European Commission and OECD initiative that defines AI literacy competencies across four domains: Engage with, Create with, Manage, and Design/Shape AI. It includes learning scenarios and serves as a basis for PISA 2029’s Machine-AI Learning Literacy assessment. The framework was developed with contributions from CodeAI (a US nonprofit) and an international expert group including researchers from INRIA (France), Spain, Canada, Uruguay, Germany, Croatia, the USA, and Italy.

inclusion.reason: This initiative qualifies for inclusion because it is formally endorsed by the European Commission (a national/sub-national government body) and the OECD (an intergovernmental body). It also includes explicit AI-literacy content through its defined competency domains and learning scenarios. The involvement of CodeAI and an international expert group further supports its credibility and reach.
